nodes.Name: Location
nodes.DocComment:
A Location maps time instants to the zone in use at that time.
Typically, the Location represents the collection of time offsets
in use in a geographical area. For many Locations the time offset varies
depending on whether daylight savings time is in use at the time instant.

Location is used to provide a time zone in a printed Time value and for
calculations involving intervals that may cross daylight savings time
boundaries.

nodes.Name: zone
nodes.DocComment: A zone represents a single time zone such as CET.

Fields.Name: isDST
Fields.DocComment: is this zone Daylight Savings Time?

nodes.Name: zoneTrans
nodes.DocComment: A zoneTrans represents a single time zone transition.

Fields.Name: when
Fields.DocComment: transition time, in seconds since 1970 GMT

Fields.Name: index
Fields.DocComment: the index of the zone that goes into effect at that time

Fields.Name: isstd
Fields.DocComment: ignored - no idea what these mean

Fields.Name: isutc
Fields.DocComment: ignored - no idea what these mean

nodes.Name: alpha
nodes.DocComment:
alpha and omega are the beginning and end of time for zone
transitions.

nodes.Name: omega
nodes.DocComment:
alpha and omega are the beginning and end of time for zone
transitions.

nodes.Name: UTC
nodes.DocComment: UTC represents Universal Coordinated Time (UTC).

nodes.Name: utcLoc
nodes.DocComment:
utcLoc is separate so that get can refer to &utcLoc
and ensure that it never returns a nil *Location,
even if a badly behaved client has changed UTC.

nodes.Name: Local
nodes.DocComment:
Local represents the system's local time zone.
On Unix systems, Local consults the TZ environment
variable to find the time zone to use. No TZ means
use the system default /etc/localtime.
TZ="" means use UTC.
TZ="foo" means use file foo in the system timezone directory.

nodes.Name: localLoc
nodes.DocComment:
localLoc is separate so that initLocal can initialize
it even if a client has changed Local.

nodes.Name: String
nodes.DocComment:
String returns a descriptive name for the time zone information,
corresponding to the name argument to [LoadLocation] or [FixedZone].

nodes.Name: FixedZone
nodes.DocComment:
FixedZone returns a [Location] that always uses
the given zone name and offset (seconds east of UTC).

nodes.Name: lookup
nodes.DocComment:
lookup returns information about the time zone in use at an
instant in time expressed as seconds since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

The returned information gives the name of the zone (such as "CET"),
the start and end times bracketing sec when that zone is in effect,
the offset in seconds east of UTC (such as -5*60*60), and whether
the daylight savings is being observed at that time.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: zone != nil && l.cacheStart <= sec && sec < l.cacheEnd

nodes.Name: lookupFirstZone
nodes.DocComment:
lookupFirstZone returns the index of the time zone to use for times
before the first transition time, or when there are no transition
times.

The reference implementation in localtime.c from
https://www.iana.org/time-zones/repository/releases/tzcode2013g.tar.gz
implements the following algorithm for these cases:
 1. If the first zone is unused by the transitions, use it.
 2. Otherwise, if there are transition times, and the first
    transition is to a zone in daylight time, find the first
    non-daylight-time zone before and closest to the first transition
    zone.
 3. Otherwise, use the first zone that is not daylight time, if
    there is one.
 4. Otherwise, use the first zone.

nodes.Name: firstZoneUsed
nodes.DocComment:
firstZoneUsed reports whether the first zone is used by some
transition.

nodes.Name: tzset
nodes.DocComment:
tzset takes a timezone string like the one found in the TZ environment
variable, the time of the last time zone transition expressed as seconds
since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC, and a time expressed the same way.
We call this a tzset string since in C the function tzset reads TZ.
The return values are as for lookup, plus ok which reports whether the
parse succeeded.

nodes.Name: tzsetName
nodes.DocComment:
tzsetName returns the timezone name at the start of the tzset string s,
and the remainder of s, and reports whether the parsing is OK.

nodes.Name: tzsetOffset
nodes.DocComment:
tzsetOffset returns the timezone offset at the start of the tzset string s,
and the remainder of s, and reports whether the parsing is OK.
The timezone offset is returned as a number of seconds.

nodes.Name: ruleKind
nodes.DocComment: ruleKind is the kinds of rules that can be seen in a tzset string.

nodes.Name: rule
nodes.DocComment: rule is a rule read from a tzset string.

nodes.Name: tzsetRule
nodes.DocComment:
tzsetRule parses a rule from a tzset string.
It returns the rule, and the remainder of the string, and reports success.

nodes.Name: tzsetNum
nodes.DocComment:
tzsetNum parses a number from a tzset string.
It returns the number, and the remainder of the string, and reports success.
The number must be between min and max.

nodes.Name: tzruleTime
nodes.DocComment:
tzruleTime takes a year, a rule, and a timezone offset,
and returns the number of seconds since the start of the year
that the rule takes effect.

nodes.Name: lookupName
nodes.DocComment:
lookupName returns information about the time zone with
the given name (such as "EST") at the given pseudo-Unix time
(what the given time of day would be in UTC).

nodes.Name: LoadLocation
nodes.DocComment:
LoadLocation returns the Location with the given name.

If the name is "" or "UTC", LoadLocation returns UTC.
If the name is "Local", LoadLocation returns Local.

Otherwise, the name is taken to be a location name corresponding to a file
in the IANA Time Zone database, such as "America/New_York".

LoadLocation looks for the IANA Time Zone database in the following
locations in order:

  - the directory or uncompressed zip file named by the ZONEINFO environment variable
  - on a Unix system, the system standard installation location
  - $GOROOT/lib/time/zoneinfo.zip
  - the time/tzdata package, if it was imported

nodes.Name: containsDotDot
nodes.DocComment: containsDotDot reports whether s contains "..".
